title: The Sacred Armour of Antiriad
build: one-file crack on a D64, packed in five stages behind 1986 SYS2080 SCI 666 (archive.org d64_Sacred_Armour_of_Antiriad_The_1986_Palace_Software, MD5 dadadbe50ae657af3f5441497c44d6de)

accuracy.note: 60 hand-written comments (13 wrong) and 20 generated (2 wrong); 14 more corrected with them, those that shared their beliefs

the room $40 widget on Discoveries, against the game running: the wait of the creatures held back by a striped one, given in steps, is 100 frames; the panel's message strip on How it works, against a screenshot of the game: drawn in hires red, it is multicolour, dark grey, light blue and cyan

exclude: runtime: zero page, stack and pages 2-3 (the shadow sprite and SID registers, the sprite slots, the animated tiles and the music), set by the start-up and the routines that use them

runtime: the sprite pictures saved while they dissolve, char_colour, cells_taken, the message queue, the add-on flags and the score; cleared by clear_game_state and written in play (at the hand-over it holds bytes left by the unpacking)
never read: eight bytes after the last animated tile script, which no pointer reaches
never read: $FF fill after the nine dissolve masks
never read: zeros after the 69 room maps; the first 32 would be the map of room $45, which only room $32's way down names, through a floor drawn solid all along
never read: $FF fill after the 748 shapes of the shape pool
never read: $0B fill after the 748 colours of the colour pool
never read: leftover bytes after the last character list

runtime: the screen and the sprite pointers; the bytes there at the hand-over are leftovers of the unpacking that clear_screen overwrites before anything reads them (a load watch on the range from the hand-over stayed silent for ten seconds, orientation.md)

runtime: panel characters $E8-$FF, built in play (score digits, energy bars, message strip), and the playfield character set at $7800, filled from the title set and then from each room's character list
never read: zeros after the colour tables

not the game's: under colour RAM, a short routine left from before the game starts ($D800-$D852: it moves memory with all RAM switched in, then loads a file from device 1 through the KERNAL and jumps through $0302), then fill; the game switches the I/O chips out only in copy_charset_from_io_ram, which reads $D000-$D7FF
never read: leftover bytes after the last animation
runtime: the NMI, reset and IRQ vectors, written by cold_start
include: RAM under the I/O area: the title screen's character set, read with $01 = 0 by copy_charset_from_io_ram

regions: zero page, the stack, the sprite slots, the music state, the score
falling drops, score weights, Geiger clicks and the animated-tile scripts

the colours of the pool's shapes
the screen and the sprite pointers
panel characters built in play, the playfield character set
creature points and damage, sounds, start places, jump steps
